I or T: A1 [ I or T ] to get something by paying money for it

NONE: › to pay someone or do something for someone, so that that person does not tell anyone something that they know about and that you want to remain secret
（做某事或付款以）封住…的嘴

T: › [ T ] informal to believe that something is true

NONE: › to be worth/not be worth the price
（買賣）合算／不合算

example: Eventually she had saved enough money to buy a small car.
她最終存夠了買一輛小汽車的錢。
[ + two objects ] He bought his mother some flowers/He bought some flowers for his mother.
他給母親買了些花。
There are more people buying at this time of the year so prices are high.
這個季節購物的人比較多，所以價格高。
The company was set up to buy and sell shares on behalf of investors.
成立該公司為的是代表投資者買賣股票。
I bought my camera from a friend of mine.
我的相機是從一個朋友處買的。
What will we have to do to buy her silence?
為了封住她的嘴我們該怎麽辦？
She'll never buy that story about you getting lost!
她決不會相信你迷路的謊話！

NONE: › disapproving to completely believe in a set of ideas
完全相信
› to buy a part of a business in order to have some control over it
買進（某公司的一部分）以實現對其的控制權

example: I don't buy into all that New Age stuff.
我根本不相信那些甚麽新思潮。
McDowell was trying to buy into the newspaper business.
麥克道爾在試圖透過收購方式進入報業。

NONE: › to pay someone so that they do not cause you any trouble
買通，賄賂

example: They tried to buy the guard at the bank off but he told the police and the gang was arrested.
那夥人試圖買通銀行的保安，但保安報了警，於是他們都被抓了起來。

NONE: › to buy a part of a company or building from someone else so that you own all of it
買斷（…的）股份（或産權）

example: Allied Chemicals have been trying to buy out their competitor's share in the target company.
聯合化工公司一直在試圖買下其競爭對手在他們想要收購的公司的股份。

NONE: › to buy something for future use and not because you need it now
預先買進

example: We bought in lots of tinned food in case of heavy snow.
我們買了許多罐裝食品以備大雪時用。

NONE: › To buy something up is to buy large amounts of it, or all that is available.
大量買進；全數買進

example: He bought up all the land in the surrounding area.
他買下了周圍地區的全部土地。

NONE: › to do something in order to be allowed more time
贏得時間；拖延時間

example: He tried to buy time by saying he hadn't been well.
他試圖以身體不適為藉口來拖延時間。

NONE: › If you buy yourself out of the armed forces, you pay an amount of money so that you can leave earlier than you had previously agreed to.
出錢以獲准提前退役

C: › [ C ] a situation in which a person or group buys enough shares in a company to get control of it
› [ C ] a situation in which a company buys its own shares from shareholders
U: › [ U ] the fact of agreeing with and accepting something that someone suggests

example: She led a buy-in of the group and is now its director.
她領導了對集團的收購，現在已成為其董事。
If you want to go ahead with these plans, you'll need buy-in from the employees.
如果你想開展這些計畫，你必須得到員工的讚同。

NONE: › an arrangement in which a business or person sells something, especially shares in companies, and then buys them again according to an agreement
（尤指股票的）回購

example: His company have just announced a $1 billion stock buyback.
他的公司剛剛宣佈回購了十億美元的股票。

NONE: B1 someone who buys something expensive such as a house
購買者，買主
› someone whose job it is to decide what will be bought by a company
買手，採購員，採買人員

example: He's still looking for a buyer for his house.
他還在給自己的房子尋找買家。
She's the buyer for a stylish boutique in Dublin.
她是都柏林一家時尚精品店的採購員。

NONE: › a time when there are more goods for sale than there are people to buy them, so prices are usually low
買方市場
› (in business) a situation in which a person or group buys all the shares belonging to a company and so gets control of it
（商業上的）控制股權收購

example: a management buyout
管理層收購
